Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary on Thursday distributed ration cards to BPL families and new PDS licences to shopkeepers at Gyan Bhawan in Patna. While distributing the cards, he congratulated recipients but vowed to fight for the bigger goal of achieving PM Narendra Modi and former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar's visions of Viksit Bharat and Samriddha Bihar, respectively. "I congratulate and thank everyone. My goal is much bigger. I will be happy when Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s dream of a developed India and Nitish Kumar’s vision of a prosperous Bihar are fulfilled," CM Chaudhary said as per a press release. "We must take a pledge that no poor person in Bihar should ever sleep hungry. Every poor person should have a ration card," the CM urged all present on the occasion. "If India has to become a developed nation by 2047, we must work towards that goal. So far, 2 crore 9 lakh ration cards have been issued across Bihar. With a ration card, you will no longer have to worry about food. The government will provide you with ration, and your food-related worries will be taken care of," he added. Claiming that the Bihar government had 24 lakh people in this scheme, the Chief Minister stressed that even after this, many families do not have ration cards. He further urged them to apply for one. "Your ration card will be issued within 30 days, and you will receive all the benefits through it," he said. Adding, CM Chaudhary also focused on other works that the BJP-JDU government has achieved over the years in Bihar, including enrolment of crores of people in the Ayushman Bharat Scheme. "We made a policy in 2024 to connect everyone with Ayushman Bharat cards so that they could receive healthcare benefits. Speaking on the winning formula of elections, CM Chaudhary said, "We provide 125 units of free electricity to 1.92 crore people in villages. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar extends deadline for free sugarcane seed scheme applications to November 25
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Top News Trendings Patna: The Bihar Sugarcane Industry Department has extended the deadline for farmers to apply for its free sugarcane seed distribution scheme, aimed at expanding cultivation in new areas. Farmers can now submit their applications online through the Cane Care portal until November 25, Jagran reported. Under the scheme, farmers will receive free, improved-quality and disease-free sugarcane seeds. The state government will also bear the transportation costs, including loading and unloading, to ensure that the seeds are delivered to farmers’ fields. The scheme is open to farmers in both sugar mill and non-sugar mill areas. In areas served by sugar mills, tenant and non-tenant farmers from villages where sugarcane is not currently cultivated and the total area under the crop is five acres or less are eligible to apply. These villages have been identified as sugarcane-free villages on the Cane Care portal. In areas where no sugar mill is currently operational, all tenant and non-tenant farmers are eligible to benefit from the scheme. Farmers will be provided free seeds for cultivating sugarcane on a minimum area of 0.25 acre and a maximum of 2.5 acres. The department has urged eligible farmers to complete the online application process by November 25 to avail themselves of the benefits. Applications can be submitted through the Cane Care portal.

bihar_raw_news.title: Supreme Court Gold Possession Rule: Explain Source During IT Raids - Bhaskar English
bihar_raw_news.content: English News National Supreme Court Gold Possession Rule: Explain Source During IT Raids | India 'Women must explain source of gold kept at home': SC says 500-gram limit offers no exemption, asks them to disclose its origin during raids New Delhi 11 hours ago Copy link For several years, the rule in the country has been that if the Income Tax Department conducts a raid, officials cannot seize up to 500 grams of gold found in the possession of a married woman. Taking advantage of this rule, many people assumed that no one would have to provide any explanation for possessing up to 500 grams of gold. However, the Supreme Court has now issued a major clarification. A bench of Justice KV Viswanathan and Justice Arun Palli said, "Non-seizure of gold and ownership of it are two different matters." The ruling came in the case of a former Bihar official who was accused of corruption. She had tried to evade action by citing her possession of 500 grams of gold. What is the full case? A disproportionate assets case was brought against former Bihar Child Development Project Officer (CDPO) Phoolpari Kumari. The Bihar Vigilance Department registered the case against her in 2015. Investigators found 646.400 grams of gold jewellery in her possession. She argued that 500 grams of gold for a married woman and 250 grams for an unmarried daughter were exempt from seizure. The Patna High Court quashed the proceedings against her in May. The Bihar government challenged this in the Supreme Court. A bench comprising Justice K.V. Viswanathan and Justice Arun Palli has now overturned the High Court's decision and restored the proceedings in the case against her. Rules on gold kept at home: 4 questions and answers Question: What are the rules regarding gold kept at home? Answer: During an income tax raid, gold will not be seized if a married woman possesses up to 500 grams, an unmarried woman up to 250 grams and a man up to 100 grams. Question: Is there any limit? Answer: No upper limit has been prescribed. Families may legally keep more than 500 grams of gold, provided they can prove that it was purchased with legitimate income. Question: How should the ruling be understood? Answer: The Supreme Court has not asked every ordinary citizen to provide an account of their jewellery. Nor has it removed the rule that provides protection against seizure. Question: What should ordinary people do? Answer: Keep the bills and receipts for your old or new jewellery, wedding invitations and documents relating to inherited jewellery safely. People are not asked to produce a bill for every piece of old or ancestral jewellery. .

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Government Increases DA for Employees and Pensioners - Udaipur Kiran
bihar_raw_news.content: Patna, November 12: The Bihar government has granted a significant relief to state employees, pensioners, and family pensioners by approving an increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR). The DA/DR under the 7th Pay Commission has been raised from 60% to 63%, with similar increases for those under the 6th and 5th Pay Commissions. The new rates will come into effect from July 1, 2026, meaning eligible employees and pensioners will also benefit from arrears based on the increased DA and DR. DA for 7th Pay Commission Employees Increased to 63% According to a report, following the Bihar Cabinet’s decision, employees and pensioners under the 7th Pay Commission will receive an additional 3% in DA/DR. Previously, the DA and DR rate was 60%, which has now been raised to 63%. This increase will take effect from July 1, 2026. For instance, if an employee has a basic pay of ₹30,000, they previously received ₹18,000 as DA at the 60% rate. With the new 63% rate, this amount will increase to ₹18,900, resulting in a monthly DA increase of ₹900. However, the actual benefit will depend on the employee’s basic pay and salary structure. Benefits for 6th and 5th Pay Commission Employees The Bihar government has also raised the DA and DR for employees and pensioners under the older pay commissions. Pay Commission Previous DA/DR New Rate Increase 7th Pay Commission 60% 63% 3% 6th Pay Commission 262% 269% 7% 5th Pay Commission 483% 497% 14% This decision will benefit state government employees, pensioners, and family pensioners who fall under the respective pay structures. The government has made the new DA and DR rates effective from July 1, 2026. This means that employees and pensioners who have been receiving payments based on the old rates may also receive the difference for the previous period according to the rules. However, the timeline and method for the payment of arrears will depend on the government’s detailed orders and departmental processes. Additionally, the Bihar Cabinet has approved the implementation of the Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) scheme for regular employees of urban local bodies. This decision aims to provide financial progress to employees who have been working in the same position for a long time without adequate promotion opportunities. The government hopes this will boost employee morale and enhance their efficiency and commitment to their responsibilities. The Cabinet has also decided to launch the ‘Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme’ to promote innovation and entrepreneurship among female students in higher educational institutions. The scheme aims to benefit up to 2,100 female students and will be implemented over four financial years from the current fiscal year to FY30, with an administrative approval of ₹88.20 crores. This initiative aims to help female students transform their new and innovative ideas into practical business models. bihar_raw_news.title: Centre to introduce evening courts in Delhi, Bihar and Andhra Pradesh on pilot basis to ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Court News Updates Courts Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Linkedin The Union Government is planning to introduce evening courts on a pilot basis in Delhi, Bihar and Andhra Pradesh as part of its efforts to address the mounting pendency of cases across the country. Under the proposed initiative, courts presently functioning during regular daytime hours will extend their working hours by a few additional hours into the evening to take up pending matters and facilitate their faster disposal. The initiative is aimed at augmenting the existing judicial infrastructure by making greater use of available court facilities beyond conventional working hours, thereby creating additional opportunities for hearing cases without necessarily requiring the establishment of entirely new courts. The proposal, announced by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice Arjun Ram Meghwal, also envisages engaging retired judges to preside over the additional evening proceedings. The project will be implemented in coordination with the respective High Courts and is expected to commence shortly. The government will assess the outcome of the pilot initiative before considering its extension to other States and Union Territories. Meghwal also underlined the importance of strengthening alternative dispute resolution mechanisms, including Lok Adalats and mediation, to facilitate settlements outside conventional court proceedings. The Centre is additionally focusing on pre-mediation to resolve disputes before they escalate into protracted litigation.

bihar_raw_news.title: Patna's 'State First Clean City' award a proud achievement for Bihar : CM Samrat Choudhary
bihar_raw_news.content: Patna's 'State First Clean City' award a proud achievement for Bihar: CM Samrat Choudhary ANI 12 Nov 2026, 00:09 GMT+10 Patna (Bihar) [India], November 11 (ANI): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday congratulated the residents of Patna after the city received the 'State First Clean City' award in the 10th edition of Swachh Survekshan 2025-26, describing the recognition as a proud achievement for the state. According to an official statement, he said receiving the award from President Droupadi Murmu was a matter of special pride for Patna and credited the achievement to collective efforts, public participation and the dedication of sanitation workers. The Chief Minister expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his continued guidance and support for Bihar's development, saying the state was achieving new milestones in development, cleanliness and urban infrastructure under his leadership. Choudhary extended his congratulations and best wishes to Patna residents, councillors, officials of the Patna Municipal Corporation and sanitation workers, acknowledging their contribution to the city's recognition. He said the hard work, dedication and commitment of sanitation workers had played a vital role in achieving the honour, while public awareness and participation had also contributed to the efforts towards cleanliness. The Chief Minister said cleanliness was not merely a campaign but the foundation for building a healthy and developed society. He added that the state government was committed to making all cities in Bihar clean, beautiful, well-organised, modern and developed. He said the government would further empower urban local bodies and ensure active citizen participation in its efforts to improve urban infrastructure and sanitation. Choudhary expressed confidence that Patna's achievement would inspire other cities in Bihar and that collective efforts would help the state reach new milestones in cleanliness and urban development. national_raw_news.content: Union Cabinet has approved the development of the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum in the North and South Block complex in New Delhi. Briefing the media after the Union Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said, the museum will integrate contemporary museum practices, immersive technologies and visitor-centric interpretation. The Cabinet has also approved the Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for RABI Season, 2026-27 on Phosphatic and Potassic fertilisers. The tentative budgetary requirement for Rabi 2026-27 will be approximately 62 thousand 370 crore rupees. This is nearly 24 thousand 417 crore more than the budgetary requirement for Rabi 2025-26 season. Mr Vaishnaw said the subsidy will ensure smooth availability of these fertilisers to the farmers at affordable prices. Mr. Vaishnaw said, the Cabinet has approved the continuation of Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units under Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031. He said that the outlay of five thousand crore rupees is approved for guarantee and it is expected to support Mudra loans worth 12.60 lakh crore rupees. The Cabinet has also given nod to the continuation of Stand-Up India Scheme for a period of five years upto 31st of March 2031. The scheme aims to promote entrepreneurship among Women, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and aims to provide financial assistance to an additional 2.5 lakh entrepreneurs in a span of five years. The Cabinet has also cleared the extension of Aqua Line Metro Rail Corridor from Noida Sector-51 to Greater Noida Sector-04 of Noida Metro Rail Project covering approximately 8.5 kilometres and comprising five elevated stations. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has stated that the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum will transform New Delhi into a global centre of cultural heritage, with the world’s largest museum display area. In a social media post, the Prime Minister noted that the Cabinet’s decision will give impetus to the transformation of the historic North and South Block buildings into a magnificent celebration of India’s civilisational journey. Mr Modi said the museum will showcase thousands of years of India’s heritage through world-class galleries and immersive experiences. It will cover a wide range of subjects, including ancient knowledge systems, mathematics, astronomy, architecture, art, languages, and spirituality. He highlighted that these buildings, which have long served as centres of governance, will now become places where millions can discover, experience, and celebrate the timeless richness of India’s civilisation. The Prime Minister described the initiative as a historic new chapter in India’s cultural heritage.

national_raw_news.title: President Droupadi Murmu awards nation's cleanest cities - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu awards nation’s cleanest cities; Visakhapatnam, Indore, Ahmedabad among top winners Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर President Droupadi Murmu awards nation’s cleanest cities; Visakhapatnam, Indore, Ahmedabad among top winners ANI | Updated: Nov 11, 2026 21:58 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], November 11 (ANI): President Droupadi Murmu presented the Swachh Survekshan 2025–26 awards on Wednesday, honouring India's cleanest urban local bodies and municipal corporations for excellence in waste management and sanitation. In the newly introduced 'Swachh Shehar Jodi' category, which pairs mentor and mentee cities to accelerate urban cleanliness, Ahmedabad and Sanand secured the top rank, followed by Indore and Deopalpur in second, and Tirupati and Kuppam in third. Navi Mumbai, Surat, and Vijayawada emerged as the top three clean cities under the Super Swachh League. Meanwhile, in the million-plus population category, Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC), Jabalpur, and Lucknow were named India's leading sanitation performers. The 2025–26 edition introduced specialised honours for riverfront, coastal, and Himalayan urban centres. According to official data, over 350 urban local bodies (ULBs) jumped more than 500 ranks from the previous cycle, with smaller municipalities playing a leading role as over 1,700 cities with populations under 50,000 improved their standings compared to 2024–25. State-level winners will be recognised during dedicated award ceremonies hosted by their respective state administrations. This year, awards were given for the first time to Swachh River Front Town, Swachh Coastal Town and Clean Himalayan City. According to a press release, President Droupadi Murmu honoured India’s cleanest cities at the Swachh Survekshan Awards 2025–26 held at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, convened by the Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Winners were felicitated in the presence of Manohar Lal, Union Minister for MoHUA & Power and Tokhan Sahu, Minister of State for MoHUA. A total of 60 national awards have been announced this year across seven distinct categories, recognising excellence in urban sanitation and waste management. The honours span the newly introduced Swachh Shehar Jodi (SSJ) category, the Clean Cities of Super Swachh League, and Swachh Shehar across five population brackets. Additional accolades celebrate top performers among Swachh River Front Towns, Swachh Coastal Towns, Clean Himalayan Cities, and State First Swachh Cities, the release stated. Speaking at the event, Droupadi Murmu underscored that cleanliness cannot be achieved through the efforts of any single institution alone and requires active participation from all stakeholders. She emphasised the importance of citizen participation, behavioural change, administrative accountability, and sustained public engagement. Highlighting the need to inculcate cleanliness values from an early age, she called for integrating issues such as plastic waste management into school curricula and fostering continuous dialogue with children and youth. The President noted that meaningful progress in sanitation is possible when citizens, local administrations, and sanitation workers work together, and when the on-ground suggestions of sanitation workers and citizen feedback are given due importance. She also appreciated the Swachh Shehar Jodi initiative as a new dimension of collaborative learning, enabling cities...

Top Stories Share DD India November 11, 2026 10:50 PM IST Prime Minister Narendra Modi | Union Home Minister Amit Shah | Government Rationalises Indian Visa Regime | Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) Government Rationalises Indian Visa Regime, Reduces Main Categories from 13 to Nine Author: DD India The Centre has rationalised India’s visa regime, reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, in a move aimed at simplifying procedures and making the system more accessible to foreign nationals visiting the country. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) implemented the latest changes on August 27, 2026, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Home Minister Amit Shah. The exercise follows an earlier rationalisation in October 2025, when the number of main categories was reduced from 22 to 13 and sub-categories from 63 to 49. The government said it had studied visa systems in developed countries and international standards while undertaking the exercise. The consolidation of categories with similar purposes is intended to provide greater clarity to applicants and facilitate legitimate foreign travel to India. Currently, e-visas are processed through electronic travel authorisation under 13 sub-categories and are available to nationals of 172 countries. Visitor Visa The erstwhile Tourist Visa has been renamed the Visitor Visa to cover a wider range of activities beyond conventional tourism. It has been divided into two sub-categories, V-1 and V-2. The V-1 Visa covers short-term activities, including business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats, short-duration medical treatment and courses in Indian languages, music, art and craft. It will be granted for 30 days with multiple entries. The V-2 Visa is intended for longer visits and will be available with a validity of one, five or 10 years, as specified. It covers activities permitted under V-1, along with mountaineering. For mountaineering, a six-month multiple-entry visa will be granted. Medical Visa The revised framework retains separate provisions for treatment under conventional and AYUSH systems. The M-1 Visa covers medical treatment other than AYUSH, while the M-3 Visa is meant for treatment under AYUSH systems. Both categories, including their e-Visa variants, will generally be granted for one year with multiple entries. Corresponding attendant visas have also been provided: M-2 for attendants accompanying M-1 visa holders and M-4 for those accompanying M-3 visa holders. The government said the provisions would offer greater flexibility to patients requiring multiple consultations, follow-up visits or staged treatment, while facilitating travel by accompanying attendants. The move is also aimed at promoting medical value tourism in line with the Prime Minister’s vision of ‘Heal in India’.
